provenance.sourceText: La taxe sur la valeur ajoutée est perçue au taux normal de 19 %.

notes:
Algeria (DZ), issue #558, transcribed 2026-09-30 from RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md. Code des Taxes sur le Chiffre d'Affaires (CTCA) 2026, art. 21 (standard 19 %) and art. 23 (reduced 9 %, quoted verbatim in vat-rates/data/dz.json, reused here rather than re-typed: see this catalog schema's own header on deliberate non-duplication). `standardRate`/`reducedRates` are set explicitly rather than left to be derived from vat-rates/, matching the convention this catalog's own header documents for a country whose rate ladder the tax engine needs directly.

SCHEMA GAP, NOT FIXED BY THIS TASK (see the stop rule in this PR's own report): Algeria's IFU (Impot Forfaitaire Unique: CIDTA art. 282bis, 'Il est etabli un impot forfaitaire unique qui couvre l'IRG, la TVA et la TLS', and art. 282ter, threshold 8,000,000 DA annual turnover) is a single flat levy that REPLACES VAT, personal income tax (IRG) and a local tax (TLS) all at once for a qualifying small business: CTCA art. 64 additionally forbids an IFU taxpayer from ever stating VAT on an invoice ('Les redevables places sous le regime de l'impot forfaitaire unique ne peuvent pas mentionner la taxe sur la valeur ajoutee sur leurs factures'). This catalog's own `schemes` field is a closed union of exactly 'STANDARD' | 'FRANCHISE_BASE' | 'EXEMPT': three VAT-holding-status variants WITHIN a VAT system, none of which represents a regime that replaces VAT with an entirely different combined tax rather than merely exempting or reducing it. `schemes` is therefore left at `['STANDARD']` here, the ordinary VAT regime this country file otherwise describes, and IFU is deliberately NOT declared as 'EXEMPT': doing so would misstate the law (an IFU taxpayer is not VAT-exempt, it is subject to a different tax altogether) for a cosmetic fit. A company actually operating under Algeria's IFU regime can still be represented in this product's EXISTING company-level 'VAT exempt' setting (`Company.exemptVat`, mapped to `taxScheme: 'FRANCHISE_BASE'` by tax/load-and-resolve.ts) to get the correct INVOICE OUTPUT (no VAT line charged, which is what CTCA art. 64 actually requires): this is a practical approximation of the OUTPUT, not a claim that IFU legally is a French-style franchise-en-base; the two are different tax mechanisms that happen to produce the same 'no VAT on the invoice' result. A faithful representation of IFU (its own combined rate, 5 % goods, 12 % other activities, 0.5 % auto-entrepreneur per CIDTA art. 282sexies, its own minimum forfaitaire, and its replacement of TWO other taxes besides VAT) has no slot in this schema today; that is the gap this PR's report names for the owner to decide on separately, per this issue's own stop rule.
